title: `AudioStreamPlayer.play()` ignores `get_tree().paused`
body:
### Tested versions

Tested and reproduced in:
* v4.2.2.stable.mono.official [15073afe3] 
* v4.3.stable.mono.official [77dcf97d8]
* v4.5.1.stable.mono.official [f62fdbde1]
* v4.6.beta3.mono.official [76dda5c6c]

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable.mono - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9144) - AMD Ryzen 9 7900X 12-Core Processor (24 threads) - 31.75 GiB memory

### Issue description

When an AudioStreamPlayer with its `process_mode` set to `Pausable` (or to `Inherit` with a pausable parent) receives a call to `play()` from an unpaused node, it plays regardless of the value of `get_tree().paused`.

### Steps to reproduce

* Create an AudioStreamPlayer with some sound to play
* Set its pause mode to Pausable
* Create another node with its pause mode set to Always
* Set `get_tree().paused = true`
* After pausing the tree, call the AudioStreamPlayer's `play()` method from the unpaused node.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

This project contains:
* an AudioStreamPlayer with an attached sound and its pause mode set to Pausable
* a button that calls the AudioStreamPlayer's `play()` method when pressed.

The main node sets `get_tree().paused = true` in its `_ready()` method, so any playback triggered by the button happens with the game tree paused. (There's a print output to ensure the paused value.)

[AudioStreamPlayerPauseBug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24478226/AudioStreamPlayerPauseBug.zip)
